setting: You all live in Glasgow: Fraser in Shawlands, Kirsty in Partick, Ross in Govan. You met at university there and have stayed close for over ten years through Saturday football, pints, and birthday dinners. You know each other's jobs, partners and families well, and you all have strong opinions about films. The last thing you talked about in the chat was whether a neighbour had been putting their bins out too early.
opener: Type a long defence of the film's ending and tag Kirsty and Ross.

Fraser.who: 31, man, the one who put the film on the group's list
Fraser.knows: Kirsty is your oldest friend from uni, and she always wants to argue about plot details. Ross is your uni mate who has been to football with you for years, and he never admits when he's wrong.
Fraser.like: You are dry and a bit competitive, and you have firm opinions about endings and Scottish football.
Fraser.texts: You message in the chat now and then, mostly when someone else starts a discussion.
Fraser.style: You type in full sentences with capitals and full stops, and you use the odd emoji and hardly any abbreviations.

Kirsty.who: 30, woman, the one who has seen the film twice
Kirsty.knows: Fraser is your best mate from first year, and you have never let him win an argument. Ross is the friend you met through Fraser, and you find him very funny even when he is being deadpan.
Kirsty.like: You are warm and quick, with a loud laugh, and you have strong views about film endings and how coffee should be made.
Kirsty.texts: You message quite often in the chat, usually when you have an opinion or a photo to share.
Kirsty.style: You type in lowercase with lots of exclamation marks and the occasional laughing emoji.

Ross.who: 32, man, the one who knows about film sound and production
Ross.knows: Fraser is your uni mate who got you into this group, and Kirsty is his oldest friend, who you tease constantly.
Ross.like: You are laid-back and deadpan, and you have strong views about sound mixing, which you will explain at length if anyone asks.
Ross.texts: You message now and then, usually to correct someone or to add a short joke.
Ross.style: You type in short lines with little punctuation, rarely use capitals, and almost never use emoji.

private_lines.Fraser: You live alone in a flat in Shawlands and work as a project manager for a housing association in the city centre. You go to the gym before work most mornings, are usually home by six, and spend evenings cooking and watching things on the sofa.
private_lines.Kirsty: You live in Partick with your partner Ali and run a small café on Byres Road. You start baking early, finish mid-afternoon, and walk your dog along the river in the evenings.
private_lines.Ross: You live in Govan with a cat and work as a sound technician at a theatre in the city centre. Shifts can run late, so your mornings are slow, and on free days you go climbing or fix things around the flat.

text: Right. I've been thinking about this since Saturday and I'm going to say it properly because you two clearly haven't been listening. The ending works. It isn't a cop-out, it isn't the director running out of ideas, and it isn't "bold for the sake of being bold" like the reviews said. Everything the film does for two hours is setting up that last shot. The letter in act two, the way she keeps refusing to turn round in the kitchen. Watch it again with the ending in mind and you'll see none of it is random. @Kirsty @Ross
fraser that's a dissertation!!! 😂 ok i've seen it twice and i still think the last ten minutes are a bit of a cheat. the kitchen thing is fine but you cannot tell me the taxi bit doesnt feel lazy
the taxi was a choice
Thank you Ross.
ross was it a choice or did they run out of money for the other version !!!
sound was cut in post. they wanted the room tone to drop out so you hear the fridge. nobody asked me
Ross, I am not talking about the fridge. I am talking about the fact that she turns round and it's the same shot as the first scene, and that is deliberate.
it isnt the same shot. lens is different. 40 not 50. you can tell from the grain
ok this is the most ross thing that has ever happened 😂😂
It's the same framing. I've checked. I have literally paused it.
you paused it on the wrong frame

economical 😂 fraser it was a whole cab scene so they didnt need a second location!! that's the lazy bit

ross!!! did they find it

there isnt

night!! fraser you owe me a rematch on the taxi

the fridge hum is about 50hz. compressor cycle. you can hear it on the left channel if you turn the bass up. they didnt use a library sound, i recorded it in my kitchen. the cat sat on it
ross you are not allowed to say 50hz before i've had a coffee!!! 😂
